record.original_question: For a fixed closed Riemannian manifold M, is there a function f_M, depending on the geometry and topology of M, such that every closed geodesic net on M of length L has at most f_M(L) balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.0.4 (Becker-Kahn). Let M be a closed Riemannian manifold. Is there a function fM (depending on geometry and topology of M) such that each closed geodesic net on M of length L has at most fM(L) (balanced) vertices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a fixed closed Riemannian manifold. A geodesic net on $M$ is a finite graph immersed in $M$ whose edges are geodesic segments and which is balanced at every interior (non-boundary) vertex, meaning that the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the outgoing edges at the vertex equals zero. A closed geodesic net is a geodesic net with no boundary vertices, i.e., the balancing condition holds at every vertex. The length of a geodesic net is the sum of the lengths of its edges.

Question: Does there exist a function $f_M : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$, depending on the geometry and topology of $M$, such that every closed geodesic net on $M$ of total length at most $L$ has at most $f_M(L)$ (balanced) vertices?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is repeatedly cited as an open question in subsequent literature on geodesic nets (e.g., works from 2020 through 2025 discussing bounds on balanced vertices in nets with few boundary vertices). Recent papers continue to study related questions and treat this Becker–Kahn-style bound for closed geodesic nets as unresolved. No proof of the conjectured bound or a counterexample appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on geodesic nets including bounds on numbers of balanced vertices.
status_evidence.claim: The question of bounding the number of balanced vertices is listed among open problems on geodesic nets.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bounds on balanced vertices in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices, treating broader bounds as open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate balanced-vertex bounds, indicating the closed-net version remains open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions showing balanced vertices can be unbounded with four boundary vertices, while the closed-net length-bounded version remains discussed as open.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research in 2025 treats the length-versus-balanced-vertex question as not yet resolved.
